items.title: fix(opencode-claimant): read session messages from /message and fail closed on unknown
items.body:
## Defect

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` read a session's messages from
`GET {OPENCODE_URL}/api/session/<id>/messages` in two places:

- `supervision_step()` — the #4758 "verify zero messages first" guard
  (before deleting a bound session and atomically rebinding its task);
- `_get_messages()` — the reconcile read `_send_prompt()` uses to decide
  whether one resend is allowed.

On the standing laptop OpenCode v2 server that path does not exist: it
returns **HTTP 404 with a zero-byte body**. Both call sites ran curl
*without* `-f` and then `json.loads(stdout or "[]")`, so the 404 parsed
to `[]` — a confirmed "zero messages" that never happened. The correct
endpoint is `GET /api/session/<id>/message`, which returns
`{"data": [ ...messages... ], "cursor": {...}}`.

## Live evidence (2026-11-09, http://127.0.0.1:13420)

Sampled four real sessions from `GET /api/session`:

```
ses_e5e40adbccfffe5tL3Wrx51oUl  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=100 at limit=100
ses_e5e403fe19cffeWYfpPV90r6Ta  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=58
ses_e5e3fbfb4a1ffeHj2ReQt5sy1v  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=17
ses_e5e403fe514ffeSDLSefGjZqEF  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=89
```

The default page is 20 messages; `?limit=100` returns the counts above,
confirming `/message` really carries the full list. (The task report
encountered 29 and 25 messages for two other sessions; the point is the
same: `/messages` 404s, `/message` 200s with `{"data": [...]}`.)

## Behavioural consequence

1. The supervision guard was **inert**. A gone/idle bound session was
   always judged "zero messages", so the loop could DELETE a session
   that actually had messages and atomically clear its task binding
   (`--launched-by opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted`),
   making the task relaunchable — the duplicate-execution defect the
   ordering exists to prevent.
2. `_get_messages()` returned `[]` instead of `None` when the read
   failed, so `_send_prompt()` could POST a second prompt into a session
   whose first prompt may already have landed.

Both docstrings already stated the intended rule: an unreadable session
is **UNKNOWN**, never empty.

## What changed

- Both paths now use `GET /api/session/<id>/message`.
- curl runs with `-f`, so any non-2xx is a failure.
- Strict parsing: only a JSON object with a **list** under `data`
  (unwrapped) or a bare JSON list is a confirmed read. Empty body,
  non-JSON, dict without a list `data`, error object, or transport
  failure returns `None` (UNKNOWN).
- `supervision_step()` now calls `_get_messages()` (one shared
  fail-closed parser) instead of its own curl/parse. `None` leaves the
  task bound — printed as a note, no DELETE, no bind. Only a confirmed
  `[]` enters the zero-message recovery path.
- Added the missing lease guard: a bound task is recoverable only once
  `poll.parse_lease_ms(task.get("lease_until"))` is in the past.
  An unparseable lease is **not** expired.
- No functions renamed, no launch/bind logic changed.

## Tests

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py` harness updated to the
`/message` endpoint and given `messages_rc` and a DELETE recorder.
New regression coverage:

- 404 / empty-body read (return code non-zero, and also a 200 with an
  empty body) → no candidate, no DELETE, no bind;
- bound session that HAS messages → not recovered;
- confirmed `{"data": []}`/`[]` → still recovers exactly as before
  (DELETE then `bind ... --launched-by
  opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted`), including the
  live 200 shape `{"data": [], "cursor": {}}`;
- bound task with an unexpired lease → not recovered;
- unparseable lease → not recovered.

Commands run (Python 3.14.8 from the user environment; no pytest):

```
python3 -m py_compile pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py
  -> COMPILE_OK

python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py
  -> Ran 15 tests in 0.035s — OK (exit 0)

python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_poll.py
  -> Ran 50 tests in 0.043s — OK (exit 0)
```

`ruff check` on the two files reports 49 findings, all pre-existing
categories (BLE001, PLW1510, UP006/UP035/UP045, DTZ003, EXE001, …); the
repo has no ruff config for this path and CI's format tier is not a
merge gate. No new finding category was introduced.

## Not verified

- I did not run the claimant in live mode against the real queue, so I
  did not observe an actual recovery fire or delete on a production
  session. The change was exercised only through the stubbed transport
  test harness plus the direct live endpoint probes above.
- I did not test a session with exactly zero messages on the live
  server (none was convenient to create); the confirmed-empty shape is
  covered by the unit tests.
- Full repository test suite was not run — only the two claimant suites.

## Open questions / defaults chosen

- Note-only handling for an unknown supervision read (a `print`, not a
  new skip record): supervision's return type is a candidate list and
  `log_fire` is not threaded into it, so recording the skip would be a
  larger change. Default: keep it a note, matching the file's existing
  warning idiom.
- Supervision reuses `_get_messages()` rather than duplicating the
  parser. This is intentional so the two reads can never diverge again.
- Lease expiry uses `time.time()` in milliseconds, matching
  `poll.is_stuck_bound`'s `now_ms` convention.

Refs #3026.

items.title: fix(pm-stack): restore opencode-claimant live implementation regressed by keeper snapshot (#6865)
items.body: Fixes #6865 (queue task 11370, lane code-q). ## What happened Keeper snapshot d0703e82ce replaced the 555-line live claimant.py with the 307-line Slice-1 shadow stub (live supervision_step returned [], launch_step only simulated), deleted test_poll.py (438 lines) — the file pm-stack-tests.yml asserts exists — and rewrote the README. ## This PR - Restores claimant.py, test_poll.py, and README.md from d0703e82ce^. - Finishes #6865 acceptance on top of the restore: top-level subprocess import (launch_step used it unimported); supervision zero-message check parses the curl subprocess result instead of an undefined requests-style messages variable; bind argv uses str(task_id); launch_step returns (launched, skips) and main() records real skips in fires.jsonl (was hard-coded []). - test_poll.py TestFetchClaimedRows reconciled to current poll.py (repo-queue list route); all other restored tests pass unchanged. - New test_claimant.py (7 tests, stubbed transport/CLI) covering launch+bind, wrong-location/cap skips, main() fire-entry skips, and supervision gone-session recovery. - pm-stack-tests.yml: test_claimant.py asserted + run alongside test_poll.py; pm-stack/opencode-claimant/** added to workflow triggers. ## Verification (laptop, this branch) - 53 tests OK (46 test_poll + 7 test_claimant). - Negative control: test_claimant.py FAILS against both the 307-line stub and 65beb42c1a claimant.py. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Eligible tasks can be launched in live mode with session creation, binding, and prompt delivery, subject to available capacity. * Live supervision checks claimed tasks and can recover eligible sessions with no messages; exhausted attempts are marked as failed when worker status is known. * Shadow mode records eligible candidates as simulated skips without creating sessions. * Launch outcomes, capacity, and skipped candidates are included in the fire log. * **Bug Fixes** * Prompt delivery retries on the same session only when a successful check confirms the session is empty.
